name: North Coast

contains: Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley

sheet.place: A huge AVA across parts of six counties north of San Francisco, with Napa and Sonoma inside it.

claims.claim: The North Coast AVA was established in 1983.
It covers parts of six counties north of San Francisco: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Solano and Sonoma.
It is a very large AVA, over 3 million acres or about 4,700 square miles.
Pacific fog and breezes cool the areas near the coast and bays. Inland valleys are much warmer, so the climate spans a wide range, from region I to IV.
It contains many smaller AVAs, including Napa Valley, Alexander Valley, Russian River Valley, Anderson Valley and Dry Creek Valley.
Many grapes grow here, including Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Zinfandel and Sauvignon Blanc.
A North Coast label lets a winery blend fruit from several counties and sub-AVAs.

terms: American Viticultural Area. A wine labeled with one must take at least 85% of its grapes from that area.

notes: Reliable warmth gives very ripe fruit and a fruit-forward style rather than an earthy or mineral one.
California Chardonnay is often buttery and full bodied, from malolactic fermentation and oak.
California Pinot Noir is generally more intense and fruity than Burgundy or Oregon.
Zinfandel is powerful and fruity, with jammy flavor.
Cabernet Sauvignon ripens fully, giving fruity, full bodied wines often above 14% alcohol.

blurb.text: A huge California AVA covering six counties north of San Francisco: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Sonoma and Solano. Pacific fog and breezes shape the weather in much of it, but its sub-appellations range from cool to warm.
